Exponentially weighted pooling does not by itself demonstrate temporal intent: with dot-product scoring, it is a weighted sum of candidate–history embedding similarities. Amazon’s [SimRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22136) demonstrates that item similarity can improve sequential recommendation, especially for rare items. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) distinguishes interaction order from elapsed time and reports benefits from modeling intervals; this supports testing timestamps, but does not establish exponential decay as the mechanism behind gains in these four categories.

Recommended discriminating controls: hold embeddings, scoring, training loss and tuning budget constant; compare last-item scoring, uniform full-history pooling, uniform recent-window pooling, event-order weights exp(−λ·events_ago), and elapsed-time weights exp(−Δt/τ). Anchor elapsed time to the last observed interaction, avoiding future-target timestamps. Include training-count popularity and normalized item-kNN baselines. Shuffle older items while retaining the last item to test information beyond immediate similarity; permute timestamp gaps while preserving item order to test elapsed-time information. These are proposed diagnostics, not published findings for this benchmark. Gains surviving popularity and similarity controls, but falling under the corresponding temporal perturbation, would support a temporal interpretation.

Build diagnostic next-item examples from prefixes within training histories, keeping official splits intact. Report paired HR@10 differences by category, history-length slice, target training-frequency bucket, and repeat versus nonrepeat target, with counts and uncertainty. [RepeatNet](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/4408) found larger improvements as repeat ratios increased, motivating this separation; if preprocessing removes repeats, report that explicitly. Require benefits on nonrepeat targets and beyond short histories before claiming broader temporal intent. Select using the pinned macro validation HR@10; training diagnostics explain mechanisms but cannot establish held-out gains.
